description:
About the Position

The Wenner-Gren Institutes at Stockholm University invite applications for a PhD student position in molecular biosciences. The institutes are the university's hub for experimental molecular biology, hosting research on gene expression, chromosome biology, infection biology, developmental systems and cellular stress responses. Doctoral researchers combine molecular and cell-biological experimentation with quantitative analysis, and the employment is a salaried four-year contract under the Swedish collective agreement.

The Wenner-Gren Institutes offer a collegial, well-equipped research environment with shared facilities, an active seminar series and links into the wider Stockholm life-science community including Science for Life Laboratory. Doctoral students define their projects with the supervisory team, receive structured training through the university's doctoral programmes and build an international publication record supporting careers in academic and industrial research.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, genetics or a related field, with hands-on laboratory experience and an interest in fundamental molecular mechanisms. Applications are submitted through Stockholm University's Varbi portal with a CV, degree certificates, reference contacts and a motivation letter; shortlisted candidates are invited for interviews with the prospective supervisor groups.

Highlights

  • PhD in molecular biosciences at the Wenner-Gren Institutes
  • Gene expression, chromosome biology and cell stress research
  • Well-equipped experimental hub with shared facilities
  • Salaried four-year employment per Swedish collective agreement
  • SciLifeLab and Stockholm life-science network
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Stockholm University

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
